decisions.reason: As a bread variant very close to the core range, rye country bread is inexpensive to continue and one year without negative signals is too little evidence to abandon the option.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen has a strong positive quality signal from the repeated gold medal, so its option value is already partly validated and warrants continuation.
Rye mixed bread with seeds fits existing production and current customer tastes, and with no clear failure signal the firm would keep this low-cost option open.
Dark barley malt rye bread uses familiar competencies and likely adds only limited assortment cost, so management would wait for more market evidence before dropping it.

Marzipan Christmas stollen is a seasonal extension close to the established confectionery business, and because keeping it available for the next season costs little there is no strong case yet for abandonment.

Ancient grain bread is a plausible artisan differentiation product aligned with the bakery’s traditional image, and despite uncertain demand the downside of continuing is limited relative to the learning value.
